text:
anya: Heads up — canary for model-eta showed a 2.2x P95 regression after the infra flip to flashv3+autotuner. Minimal repro below, seems correlated with head_dim=37 and seqlen=512, batch=8.

anya: quick profiler snapshot (sampling, 10s):
```
perf: flashv3_causal_kernel 57%
perf: sdpa_fallback 36%
perf: memcpy/overhead 7%
```

mike: repro steps? can you paste the curl or python snippet?

anya: repro (curl against local canary):
```
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"model-eta","input":"x" ,"batch":8,"seqlen":512,"head_dim":37}'
```
Also see kernel-picker log lines: `kernel_picker: head_mod=37 chosen=sdpa_fallback reason=unaligned_tile`

sasha: interesting — our headmod bucketization basically does head_dim % 8 and then picks tiled kernels only when remainder==0 or >= some threshold. primes like 37 slip the heuristic and we bounce between flashv3_causal (good raw perf) and sdpa_fallback (slow) depending on microbatch alignment. That causes KV warmup thrash + cache invalidations.

kevin: I saw similar on another model but with head_dim=19. Two ideas: (1) bump heuristic to use next_multiple(head_dim, 8) and prefer kernels that tolerate padding, (2) add a small hysteresis in the kernelpicker so transient microbatch shapes don't flip picks mid-flight.

anya: +1 for hysteresis. The profiler shows the pick flips mid-request on some RPC interleavings. Hysteresis should be time-based (ms) not just based on batch counts.

mike: concrete quickfix we can toggle from console: set REDWOOD_KERNELPICK_HYST_MS=200 and REDWOOD_PAD_HEAD_TO=8. Canary with these envs?

infra-bot: deploy/canary/7345 started by @anya — config override REDWOOD_KERNELPICK_HYST_MS=200, REDWOOD_PAD_HEAD_TO=8. Check /ops/traces/7345 for perf spans. :rocket:

anya: after toggling, 30s snapshot:
```
perf: flashv3_causal_kernel 89%
perf: sdpa_fallback 9%
perf: memcpy/overhead 2%
latency.p95 before=420ms after=180ms
```
Looks promising but we should make the kernelpicker aware of two more things: head_dim prime-ish behavior (prefer pad-over-fallback), and KV-cache alignment — when we pad keys we must update KV offset math to avoid misaligned loads.

sasha: noted. I'll open a small PR to the kernelpicker with: (a) pad preference flag, (b) pick_hysteresis_ms setting, (c) unit test for head_dim in {19,31,37,41}. Also will add a kv-offset assert to prevent misread on padded cache entries.

kevin: also worth adding a lightweight warmup at model load that issues one synthetic batch to populate the KV cache and lock in kernel choice for steady state (only for private/dedicated where we control warmup). avoids thundering transitions.

anya: created canary issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-1298 with logs and reproduction. I'll monitor canary for 24h and if stable we promote to prod with the hysteresis + pad heuristics.

mike: thanks — can we add an automatic check in autotuner that flags >20% fallback time for >10s and emits an alert? That would catch similar regressions earlier.

sasha: yes, adding alert. Also documenting in runtime/notes: "headdim-prime-edgecases.md" (internal) with mitigation checklist.

anya: TL;DR: regression root cause = kernelpicker flip + head_dim that causes mis-bucketing -> sdpa fallback. Mitigation = pad-pref + 200ms hysteresis + warmup. Rolling patch underway. :white_check_mark:
